items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: I want the rhythm section to sound like a Diana Krall record

ctx.x: Right. Well this has just been a delight for me, as an arranger myself I’m very envious of your career. And another quote – one more quote from you. “I was one of the cogs in the wheel of record producing.” You were a large cog I think.

Well you know the position that arrangers have, it’s sort of like the drummer who gets the groove on a record, and a bass player who reads the notes but makes it feel like it’s in the pocket. Any one of those guys missing could alter the outcome. And when you’re working with a team and you’re a cog in the wheel, you’re one of the ones that’s making that wheel turn. Now in some cases yeah you play a more major part than this person over here or that person over there. But in essence pretty much everything we do as…
I think it does, and it’s all worked for you. And I want to thank you for your time today. It’s enlightening and I know people are going to dig it.
